spans.s: To observe any religious obligation (such as a vow).
ज्योक् [jyōk], ind. Long, for a long time; ज्योक् च सूर्यं दृशे
ज्योग्जीवनम् [jyōgjīvanam], A longer life; स्वरवर्णप्रसादादिदर्शनादेव ज्योग्जीवनमप्यनुमास्यते ŚB. on
ज्योतिर्मय [jyōtirmaya], a. Consisting of stars, starry;
ज्योतिष [jyōtiṣa], a. (-षी f.) [ज्योतिः सूर्यादिगत्यादिकं प्रतिपाद्यतया$ स्त्यस्य अच्]
Astronomical or astrological. -षः An astronomer or astrologer.
षम् Astronomy, astrology, the science of the course of the heavenly bodies and divisions of time resting thereon; कलामात्रा- विशेषज्ञाञ् ज्योतिषे च परं गतान्
One of the six Vedāṅgas (being a short tract on astronomy).-Comp. -विद्या astronomical or astrological science.
ज्योतिषिकः [jyōtiṣikḥ], One who studies or knows astronomy.
ज्योतिषी [jyōtiṣī] ज्योतिष्कः [jyōtiṣkḥ], ज्योतिष्कः A planet, star, luminary. -ष्कम् N. of the shining peak of Meru. -ष्कः The चित्रक tree.
Luminous, bright, shining, possessed of luminous bodies; नक्षत्रतारा- ग्रहसङ्कुलापि ज्योतिष्मती चन्द्रमसैव रात्रिः
N. of the third foot of Brahmā.
N. of one of the seven suns appearing at the destruction of the world.
ती The night (as illuminated by the stars).
(In phil.) A state of mind pervaded by सत्त्वगुण i. e. a tranquil state of mind.
ज्योतिस् [jyōtis], n. [द्युत्-इसुन् आदेर्दस्य जः. ज्युत्-इसुन् वा]
Light, lustre, brightness, flash; ज्योतिरेकं जगाम Ś.5.3;
Light of Brahman, light regarded as the Supreme spirit;
;13.17; अथ यदतः परो दिवो ज्योतिर्दीप्यते Ch.
A heavenly body, a luminary (planet, star &c.); ज्योतिर्भिरुद्यद्भिरिव त्रियामा
Brightness of the sky, day-light (opp. तमस्).
Light as the divine principle of life, intelligence.
The science of the course of heavenly bodies; astronomy. See ज्योतिष.

An epithet of Viṣṇu.-Comp. -इङ्गः, -इङ्गणः the fire-fly. -कणः a spark of fire. -गणः the heavenly bodies collectively; -चक्रम् the zodiac. -ज्ञः an astronomer of astrologer. -मण्डलम् the stellar sphere. -मिलिन् m. -वी(बी)जम् a fire-fly.-रथः (ज्योतीरथः) the polar star. -लोकः the supreme spirit. -विद् m. an astronomer or astrologer. -विद्या, -शास्त्रम् (ज्योतिःशास्त्रम्) astronomy or astrology.-स्तोमः (ज्योतिष्टोमः) a Soma sacrifice considered as the type of a whole class of sacrificial ceremonies.-ज्योतिष्टोमः A kind of soma sacrifice requiring sixteen priests for its performance. -हस्ता N. of Durgā.
A moonlight-night. -Comp. -ईशः the moon. -प्रियः the Chakora bird. -वृक्षः a lamp-stand, a candle-stick.
